entries.what_happened: Two manuscripts, both claiming the numerical-dimension-one case of threefold abundance in characteristic p>3 over an algebraically closed field. (1) 'Log abundance in numerical dimension one for threefolds in positive characteristic' (dated October 5, 2026) claims: for a projective log canonical threefold pair (X,B), with X normal, B an effective Q-divisor, K_X+B Q-Cartier, nef and of numerical dimension one, K_X+B is semiample (Theorem thm:main). Neither terminality nor Q-factoriality of X is assumed. The proof is by contradiction. After reductions (a dlt model, a terminal Q-factorial model, Xu's nonvanishing giving a nonzero effective N_0 with N_0 ~ m(K+B)), it assumes the nef dimension of N_0 is three. It then separates the boundary from N_0 (BNH=0, via bend-and-break), isolates a coefficient-one component by a partial MMP, proves torsion on the nonreduced Cartier cycle (adjunction plus surface abundance), and builds a smooth threefold V with a connected primitive nef cycle D that has torsion normal bundle and a canonical relation. It then invokes a cycle obstruction theorem stated as a black box from the companion (2). Nef dimension at most two is handled by Xu's cited theorems. (2) 'Abundance in numerical dimension one for terminal threefolds in positive characteristic' (dated September 24, 2026; called the companion in (1)) claims: for a normal projective Q-factorial terminal threefold X over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>3 with K_X nef and numerical dimension one, some positive Cartier multiple of K_X has at least two independent sections, so kappa(X,K_X)=1 and K_X is semiample (Theorem thm:main). Its proof is also by contradiction in the case of nef dimension three. It builds a smooth V and a connected snc primitive nef cycle D with torsion O_D(D) and a canonical relation near D. It shows T_V strongly semistable, c_2(V)·D=0 and uniform polar-part bounds, proves a Laurent-cohomology vanishing criterion, and concludes that the Picard group of the punctured formal neighbourhood of |D| is p-divisible while a degree homomorphism to Z is nonzero on it. The final semiampleness step and nef dimension at most two are taken from Xu's cited theorems.
entries.delivers: For the bullet (klt varieties, K_X nef, semiample, no boundary, every dimension, no field restriction) the manuscripts claim exactly one slice: threefolds X of numerical dimension one, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>3. Manuscript (1) with B=0 covers every klt, indeed lc, threefold with K_X nef and nu(K_X)=1 in that setting, with no terminality or Q-factoriality hypothesis. Manuscript (2) covers the terminal Q-factorial subcase and additionally states kappa(X,K_X)=1. Neither manuscript says it settles the abundance conjecture. Both say they prove the numerical-dimension-one case of threefold (log) abundance in this characteristic range. Their problem statements differ from the bullet's: (1) states log abundance for lc pairs with effective rational boundary (the bullet is its B=0 case, restricted to threefolds); (2) states abundance only for terminal Q-factorial threefolds, which is a subclass of the bullet's klt varieties. Both are stated over algebraically closed fields, and both are restricted to p>3.
entries.remains: If the claims are correct, still open for the bullet: every dimension other than 3 (neither manuscript treats other dimensions); threefolds with nu(K_X)=0 (nef K_X numerically trivial, which needs torsion); threefolds with nu(K_X)=2 (only via Xu's 2026 theorem, cited, not proved in this family); threefolds with nu(K_X)=3 (nef and big, not treated); characteristic 0, 2 and 3 (p=2 and p=3 are excluded and characteristic 0 is not addressed); and fields that are not algebraically closed, except for the one-paragraph descent argument each manuscript gives.
entries.direction: proves a case (numerical dimension one, threefolds, characteristic p>3)
entries.conditional_on: (1) depends on the cycle obstruction theorem (Theorem thm:obstruction, 'Cycle obstruction from the companion'), which (1) states without proof as a theorem and attributes to the companion's Proposition 2.1 and Sections 3-6 (cited as Corollary 5.4 and Proposition 6.8). The matching statements in (2) appear to be its form-vanishing corollary (Section 5) and its degree contradiction (Section 6); I did not verify the numbering against a compiled version. (1) also relies on Xu's nonvanishing and abundance theorems (Xu 2024, Theorems 1.4, 1.5, 1.8), Hashizume-Nakamura-Tanaka and Hacon-Witaszek MMP results (Hacon-Witaszek Theorem 1.2), Xu 2026's partial MMP and dlt lemmas, Posva's and Tanaka's surface abundance (Posva Theorem 3.1, Tanaka Theorem 0.1), and Jovinelly-Lehmann-Riedl bend-and-break (Theorem 1.1). (2) depends on Xu 2024 Theorems 1.4, 1.6 and 1.8, Xu 2026's nef reduction and partial MMP lemmas, the threefold MMP (Hacon-Xu, Hashizume-Nakamura-Tanaka, Hacon-Witaszek), Posva's and Tanaka's surface abundance, Xu-Zhang Lemma 2.10, Jovinelly-Lehmann-Riedl bend-and-break, Langer's Bogomolov inequality, and Katz's Cartier descent. (2) does not depend on (1).
entries.doubts: (1): The contradiction rests on the companion's obstruction. (1) says it applies to 'any cycle with the displayed properties' on the grounds that the companion's Section 2 retains only V, D, H_V, the torsion order and the canonical relation (foundations.tex:50-56, 66-70). The cycle constructed in (1) comes from a different, log canonical construction, so applicability depends on that reading of the companion. Several steps are compressed: the claim that the relative MMP output is not of fibre type and still has nef dimension three is given in a few sentences (foundations.tex:145-178); the 'for completeness' argument that very general points avoid the bad set (boundary.tex:55-66) is brief; the claim that removing an effective boundary from a dlt pair strictly increases discrepancy, used to get Y klt, is asserted in one sentence (isolation.tex:213-218); the isolation step is described as adapting the companion's Section 2.3 and Xu's partial-MMP formulation. The theorem is stated for algebraically closed k, and the descent from an uncountable closure is argued in one paragraph (foundations.tex:131-143). The bend-and-break bound 0 <= N·Gamma <= 4·NC/(-KC) is taken from Jovinelly-Lehmann-Riedl as stated. (2): The paper says 'We give the details that are relevant here' for slope calculus when D is only nef, not ample (slopes.tex:28-31). It says 'One can check' for the dual of a jet map and its index (jets.tex:182) and for a base-change square (laurent.tex:408). The omitted-lift combinatorics in the jet section are described by an illustrative picture (jets.tex:676-691). The semistability proof cites Xu-Zhang Lemma 2.10 'with the quantitative bend-and-break statement specified below' (slopes.tex:325), which is then stated (slopes.tex:372-380). The final semiampleness step (from kappa=1) uses Xu 2024 Theorem 1.6, not proved here. Q-factoriality is a stated hypothesis of the theorem but is not preserved by the field extension used in the proof; the text says modifications supply it when needed (preparation.tex:119-120).
